tasks.title: formatCents in src/cents.js
tasks.description: Render a whole number of cents as a dollar string.

context.reason: the test that decides whether this task worked

edits.change: Replace the stub with formatCents(cents): it takes a finite number of whole cents and returns a dollar string with exactly two decimals, the digits before the point grouped with a comma every three digits, and a leading minus sign before the dollar sign when the value is negative. So formatCents(0) is '$0.00', formatCents(5) is '$0.05', formatCents(123456) is '$1,234.56', formatCents(100000000) is '$1,000,000.00' and formatCents(-500) is '-$5.00'. Throw a TypeError when the argument is not a finite number. formatCents stays the only export of the module.

tasks.title: slugify in src/slug.js
tasks.description: Turn a title into a url slug.

context.reason: the test that decides whether this task worked

edits.change: Replace the stub with slugify(text): lowercase the text, replace every run of characters that is not a lowercase letter or a digit with a single hyphen, then strip the hyphens from both ends. So 'Hello, World!' is 'hello-world', '  A  B  ' is 'a-b', 'Foo--Bar' is 'foo-bar', '2026 Q1' is '2026-q1' and '---' is the empty string. Throw a TypeError when the argument is not a string. slugify stays the only export of the module.

tasks.title: truncate in src/truncate.js
tasks.description: Cut a string to a limit and mark that it was cut.

context.reason: the test that decides whether this task worked

edits.change: Replace the stub with truncate(text, limit): when text.length is at most limit return text unchanged, otherwise return the first limit - 1 characters of text followed by the single character U+2026 (a horizontal ellipsis). So truncate('hello', 10) and truncate('hello', 5) are both 'hello', truncate('hello', 3) is 'he\u2026' and truncate('hello', 1) is '\u2026'. Throw a TypeError when limit is not an integer and a RangeError when limit is below 1. truncate stays the only export of the module.

tasks.title: chunk in src/chunk.js
tasks.description: Cut a list into fixed-size groups.

context.reason: the test that decides whether this task worked

edits.change: Replace the stub with chunk(items, size): group the items into consecutive arrays of size items, each one the slice of the list it covers, with the last group shorter when the list does not divide evenly and an empty list giving an empty result. So chunk([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 2) is [[1, 2], [3, 4], [5]] and chunk([], 3) is []. tasks.description: Capitalise the first letter of every word.
